title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) to measure whether inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and an emulated execution reduces the proportion of configurations that would execute with operational faults. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical LLM candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification), we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents with gpt-5-mini and a canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes (72 pairs) and 72 model calls. All baseline executions produced no emulator-observed faults (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0). The paired difference in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics this degenerate confirmatory outcome is expected when identical generated candidates produce no baseline execution faults. We present preregistration rationale, deterministic execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, exact inferential outputs, and concrete methodological recommendations for experiments able to detect verifier utility under realistic baseline-error regimes.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to translate high-level operator intents into device-level configurations for network operations (NetOps). Intent→configuration translation can accelerate change pipelines but also risks silently violating reachability, policy, ordering, or workflow invariants and causing outages if generated text is executed without further checks. A common deployment mitigation is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) architecture that pairs stochastic LLM generation with deterministic verification followed, where needed, by repair or human review. Prior empirical work demonstrates promising intent→config accuracy in constrained vendor-dialect settings [1] and prototype co-pilots that incorporate verification [2], yet systematic, preregistered experiments that measure verifier detection performance against executed outcomes are scarce [3].

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment that isolates deterministic verifier detection on identical LLM outputs under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The core research question is: does inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM generator and emulator execution materially reduce the proportion of configurations that execute with operational faults when the identical generated candidate is evaluated both without and with verification? The design intentionally isolates detection (verifier flagging) from improvements that could arise from alternate generator samples, prompt modifications, or repair-enabled iterations.

Our principal contribution is an artifact-grounded, fully archived confirmatory run (72 paired intents) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The run produced a ceiling/null result (zero baseline emulator faults), and we analyze why that outcome follows given the preregistered contract and the archived task/validator semantics. We close with concrete, artifact-supported recommendations for preregistered designs that can detect verifier utility when baseline error prevalence is non-negligible.
sections.related_work:
Research on LLM-driven NetOps spans intent-based configuration generators, tool-augmented agentic frameworks, and architectural proposals for GVR stacks. Nguyen et al. evaluate intent→configuration pipelines in emulator settings and report task-level correctness for constrained vendor dialects [1]. Multi-agent and tool-augmented frameworks for intent-driven NetOps (Confucius-style systems, co-pilots) have been proposed and prototyped; such systems commonly propose integrated verification to reduce regressions but typically omit preregistered detection-evaluations tied to emulator-executed outcomes [2].

Generate–Verify–Repair architectures have empirical precedent in software and code-generation domains where deterministic checkers and test suites validate stochastic outputs and drive repair iterations; these works motivate similar pipelines for NetOps but do not provide extensive empirical coupling with network verifiers and emulated execution outcomes [3]. Constraint-enforcing and integer-programming constrained decoding reduce structured-output violations in other domains and suggest complementary strategies to reduce generator violations in NetOps [4]. Classical deterministic network-verification methods (e.g., header-space and policy checkers) provide precise invariants (reachability, ACL semantics, ordering) and are natural verifier candidates; however, prior literature lacks preregistered paired experiments that report verifier true/false detection rates against emulator failures for identical generated candidates [5].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 and froze the design and analysis prior to observing outcomes. The primary estimand is the paired reduction in undetected operational-fault proportion (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Confirmatory H1 targeted an absolute paired reduction of 0.20 with two-sided alpha = 0.05 and power ≥ 0.80; power calculations indicated ≈63 pairs required and we preregistered N = 72 pairs (24 per topology-difficulty stratum) to provide margin for deterministic exclusions.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and experimental contract. The execution_contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial LLM generation was produced and that identical candidate was evaluated in two conditions. Baseline: execute the shared candidate in an isolated emulator and record emulator fault/no-fault. Guarded: run the canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on the same candidate; if the verifier flags violations the guarded outcome is recorded as prevented (no execution); if it does not flag, execute the identical candidate and record the emulation outcome. Because only a single shared candidate exists per intent the guarded arm cannot improve outcomes by resampling the generator; a paired difference can only arise from deterministic verification preventing an otherwise executed fault.

Model, adapter, and verifier configuration. The declared model recorded in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini (provider = openai_responses, max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1). The configuration records temperature = null; this indicates provider-default runtime sampling semantics and is archived as a residual sampling-parameter uncertainty (documented in the artifacts). The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The canonical verifier is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0"), which implements a full_intent_constraint_validation rule set that produces a binary per-episode validity verdict and structured validator_traces (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validation_before/after states, violation_codes, difficulty metadata). All verifier decisions and traces were archived per episode.

Task-bank construction, contamination controls, and stratification. Tasks were deterministically generated using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task manifest entry encodes: a natural-language intent, a machine-structured required_sequence (ordered field changes), allowed_touched_fields, initial and expected final states, and difficulty labels (medium/hard/very_hard). The preregistration mandated deterministic exact-match contamination checks against public corpora with explicit exclusion rules. analysis/contamination_summary.csv records zero exact-match exclusions for confirmatory pairs. The confirmatory sample remained stratified as preregistered (24 pairs per stratum).

Execution protocol, retries, and deterministic accounting. The missingness_plan allowed up to two additional retries (3 attempts total) for transient hosted-API errors for generation calls; execution metadata logs all retries and provider-call events. The run started at 2026-08-31T06:56:23.065707Z and completed at 2026-08-31T07:06:28.665518Z (≈10.1 minutes wall-clock). The execution manifest reports planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 72 (shared initial generation per pair). Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 72, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 72, cache_miss_count = 72, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 72}.

Scoring and inferential procedures. Each episode's verifier outputs a score and validator_trace; the primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 to form the 2×2 paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) and applied an exact McNemar two-sided test when discordant pairs exist. We computed paired bootstrap-percentile 95% confidence intervals for the paired difference using 10,000 resamples with bootstrap_seed = 1729 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Pre-specified subgroup confirmatory comparisons (topology complexity and policy type) were registered with Holm correction; these become non-informative in the absence of discordant pairs but are archived for reproducibility.
sections.results:
Execution and manifest summary. The autonomous pipeline completed without technical failures. Key manifest figures: planned_episode_count = 144; completed_episode_count = 144; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 72; artifact_count = 510. analysis/condition_summary.csv records baseline successes = 72, baseline failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded successes = 72, guarded failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0).

Paired contingency and exact inference. Aggregating across the 72 confirmatory pairs produced contingency counts n_11 = 72, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (guarded × baseline). The paired estimate paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) is [0.0, 0.0], reflecting the degenerate distribution produced by the absence of discordant pairs. analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv contain these tabulations.

Representative validator diagnostics. Representative per-episode scoring artifacts are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json). Across these examples validator_trace fields show parsed_command_count between 2 and 6, required_command_count matching parsed counts for valid sequences, difficulty.level spanning medium/hard/very_hard, normalized_configuration matching the shared candidate, validator_version = "5.0", score_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION", and violation_count = 0. These traces confirm the verifier executed on each shared candidate and produced no violation flags on the preregistered tasks.

Contamination, missingness, and sensitivity diagnostics. analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports zero exact-match contaminations for confirmatory pairs. analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 72 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses (treating excluded pairs as failures; bootstrap diagnostics) were executed and archived: because no pairs were excluded and no discordant outcomes occurred these sensitivity analyses reproduce the degenerate numeric conclusion (paired difference = 0.0).
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory interpretation. The preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics validly measures verifier detection on identical candidates. Observing zero baseline faults yields a scientifically informative ceiling/null outcome: given the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), prompt/templates, and synthetic task bank the generator outputs were uniformly valid in the emulator; therefore the verifier had no executed failures to prevent. The numerical outputs (n_11 = 72; paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap CI [0.0,0.0]) are direct consequences of the preregistered contract and observed data and therefore correctly reported as a degenerate confirmatory result.

Artifact-grounded causes of the ceiling outcome. Several archived, measurable factors contributed to the ceiling outcome: (1) the deterministic task generator produced constrained, high-clarity intents with explicit required_sequence fields and allowed_touched_fields encoded in each task manifest, increasing the likelihood of unambiguous correct candidates; (2) gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json) generated sequences that matched those structured constraints across the synthetic corpus; and (3) the verifier rule set (full_intent_constraint_validation in deterministic_netops_validator_v5) aligns closely with the required_sequence constraints present in the task manifests, making verification and generation objectives strongly congruent. These artifact-supported factors together explain why baseline emulator executions produced no faults for the selected corpus.

Implications for future confirmatory designs. To empirically measure practical verifier benefits we recommend preregistered designs that raise baseline error prevalence or permit verifier-mediated candidate changes. Artifact-grounded alternatives supported by the same executor include: (A) independent-generation arms—allow separate initial generations per condition so verifier-triggered repairs or alternative sampling may change executed candidate distributions; (B) repair-enabled flows—permit a single deterministic repair call when the verifier flags violations and execute repaired candidates, measuring end-to-end improvement; (C) adversarial/fault-injection task banks—seed tasks with ambiguous intents, ordering subtleties, or protocol edge cases to elevate baseline error prevalence and reveal detection tradeoffs; (D) multi-model and sampling sweeps—include multiple model versions and explicit sampling parameter settings (non-null temperatures) to quantify model- and sampling-sensitivity. All these alternatives are compatible with the archived execution and analysis infrastructure and can be preregistered using the same evidence-recording conventions.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolates detection but prevents verifier-mediated candidate selection from influencing outcomes; this design choice trades sensitivity to repair-mediated benefit for clarity of detection measurement. Construct validity: emulator-observed faults are a conservative proxy for operational harm but do not capture traffic-dependent timing or device-specific emergent failures in production. External validity: experiments used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic task bank, and one deterministic verifier; extrapolation to other models, vendor dialects, or production hardware is limited. Conclusion validity: because baseline error prevalence was zero in this corpus the confirmatory design had no power to detect verifier benefit here. Residual uncertainty: contamination checks found no exact-match contamination but private hosted-model training data remains a possible source of undetected leakage and is an acknowledged residual uncertainty.

Operational implications and measured tradeoffs. The confirmed ceiling outcome does not imply verifiers are unnecessary; rather, it shows that under certain tightly constrained synthesis/evaluation conditions an LLM alone produced valid device sequences. In operational settings where intents are ambiguous, task constraints are incomplete, or vendor dialects vary, verifiers remain a mechanistic guard. Measuring verifier cost (false positives that block safe changes) and benefit (true positives preventing faults) requires task banks with non-negligible baseline failure prevalence; the archived artifacts and preregistration provide a reproducible template for such follow-on evaluations.

Reproducibility and artifact availability. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle. Key artifacts referenced in the manuscript include execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, deterministic_reconciliation.json, and per-episode validator traces under execution/scoring/. The analysis bootstrap used seed = 1729 and 10,000 resamples; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records these values. The run-level timing, provider-call audit, and artifact counts are recorded in execution/ and analysis/ manifests to enable deterministic reconciliation of the paired accounting.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure whether a canonical deterministic verifier reduces the proportion of LLM-generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. For the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic/emulated task bank, baseline executions produced zero emulator faults and the verifier did not change outcomes (paired difference = 0.0; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). This artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome is internally consistent with the preregistered design: when identical generated candidates produce no executed faults a verifier cannot reduce executed faults under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Measuring verifier utility under realistic error regimes requires experimental contracts that permit independent or multiple generator samples, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, and multi-model comparisons. The archived artifacts (responses, task manifests, verifier traces, execution manifest, and complete analysis logs) provide a reproducible baseline and a template for those follow-on confirmatory designs and power calculations (preregistration targeted N≈63 pairs for a 0.20 absolute reduction; N=72 was used to provide margin).

limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per‑condition generation, multi‑sample generation, or repairs unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single‑model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.

Sampling‑parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (sampling parameters unset); null indicates provider default sampling semantics determined runtime sampling behavior and is a residual uncertainty recorded in the archived configuration.

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact‑match checks were applied, but private training‑data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
